questions.question: OP-01's record has 22 open items for a reopen session (O14 to O44, from audit-025 and this review), but /observe has no mode for deciding open items. How should the reopen run?

options.label: File BK-501 first (Recommended)
options.description: A small tooling PR adds a reopen mode to /observe: one dialog per open item, the answer recorded as a new decision D45+ naming what it amends, then /observe-review again. The reopen session follows in a fresh session.

options.label: Reopen ad hoc now
options.description: Run a fresh armed /observe OP-01 and walk the open items by hand under the existing rules. Faster, but nothing defines the steps, so the session invents them, the failure mode RFC-0028 was written to close.

options.label: Spec first, reopen later
options.description: Write step 5's spec from the decisions no open item names, and leave the reopened clauses out until a later session. Against RFC-0028 P3 for the affected clauses; the spec is partial.

questions.question: BK-501 (an /observe reopen mode that decides a record's open items) is filed on branch bk-501-observe-reopen. What should this branch deliver?
BK-501: how does an /observe session know it is a reopen? The hook arms on `/observe <entry> [path ...]` and refuses any extra word that is not a file.

options.label: By the record's state (Recommended)
options.description: `/observe OP-01` on a record whose Status is Complete walks its open items. A Complete record has no axis left to continue, so the mode is unambiguous. No hook change, and the hook tests stay as they are.

options.label: Explicit keyword
options.description: `/observe OP-01 reopen`. The hook learns the keyword, and tests pin it. The mode is visible in the prompt, but the change touches observe_ground.py's arm and rearm parsing.

questions.question: BK-501: how does the reopen session's answer to an open item land in the record?

options.label: New decision plus pointers (Recommended)
options.description: Each answer is a new decision, D45 onward, with an `Amends:` line naming the decisions it changes. Each amended decision gains one `Amended by:` line, and nothing else in it changes. The item gains `Decided by:` and stays listed. History stays in the record, and the spec finds the current text from the old decision.

options.label: New decision only
options.description: Same new decisions D45 onward, but old decisions stay byte for byte. A reader of D35 must search later decisions to learn it was amended.

options.label: Edit in place
options.description: The old decision's text is rewritten and the item removed. The shortest record, but the history lives in git only, and the Asked pairing of the old decision breaks.

questions.question: BK-501: which open items does a reopen session walk? For OP-01 the full set would be the 22 reopens and gaps plus 7 notes (O18, O23, O29, O30, O32, O38, O40).

options.label: Reopens, gaps and notes (Recommended)
options.description: Every open item that names a decision of this record to decide. It skips items tagged `shared:`, items addressed to another entry's session (O1, O2, O6, O13, O42) and ground conflicts (O21, which runs spec 051's flow). A note is asked too, and its answer may be 'leave as is'.

options.label: Reopens and gaps only
options.description: The 22 that block spec clauses. Notes stay open for whoever writes the spec. A shorter session, but the notes' wording questions stay undecided.

questions.question: BK-501: what happens to the record during and after a reopen session?

options.label: In progress, then review again (Recommended)
options.description: Status goes to In progress when the session starts. The End pass reruns, then Status returns to Complete, and /observe-review reruns on the whole record. Its pairs check sees the new decisions' Asked lines, and its readers catch new-against-old conflicts.

options.label: Review the new decisions only
options.description: The same status handling, but /observe-review pairs and reads D45 onward only. Cheaper, but it misses a conflict between a new decision and an old one, the class 1 that RFC-0028's readers exist for.

options.label: No second review
options.description: Status returns to Complete and the spec follows directly. The fastest path, but the new decisions get no check after their session.
